title: Discrete power-law decay of subsystem distance after a quantum quench
abstract: We present a numerical study of subsystem distance decay following a global quantum quench in the infinite one-dimensional transverse-field Ising chain, using the mathematically rigorous Bures distance $B_A(t)$ to quantify the deviation of the time-evolved reduced density matrix from its stationary generalized Gibbs ensemble state. We show that the late-time decay follows a discrete power law $B_A(t) \sim t^{-λ}$, with the exponent $λ$ confined to discrete values: $1$, $5/4$, $3/2$, $7/4$, $2$, $5/2$, and potentially further values. The specific exponent is jointly determined by the pre- and post-quench transverse fields, as well as by properties of the symmetric excitation-fraction function $m_S(\varphi)$, defined on $\varphi\in[0,π]$ to characterize the pre-quench Hamiltonian eigenstates, including continuity, boundary values, and first-derivative boundary values, among others. The previously established $t^{-3/2}$ decay for the initial ground state of the pre-quench Hamiltonian is naturally recovered as a special case of this general classification. Our results reveal a universal discrete structure governing local equilibration dynamics in integrable quantum systems.
summary: The paper analyzes the late-time relaxation of subsystem correlations following a quantum quench in the 1D transverse-field Ising chain. Using the Bures distance, they demonstrate that this decay follows a discrete power law $t^{-\lambda}$. The exponent $\lambda$ is not arbitrary but is rigidly determined by the specific parameters defining the initial and final states, revealing universal structure in local equilibration dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how local quantum correlations decay over time following a global quench in an integrable many-body system.
main_result: The subsystem distance decays universally according to a discrete power law, $B_A(t) \sim t^{-\lambda}$, where the exponent $\lambda$ is restricted to specific rational values determined by the initial and final Hamiltonian parameters.
method: The analysis uses numerical simulations of the Bures distance between the time-evolved reduced density matrix and its generalized Gibbs ensemble counterpart.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the infinite one-dimensional transverse-field Ising chain, governed by a Hamiltonian dependent on pre-quench ($h_0$) and post-quench ($h$) transverse fields. The quench involves evolving an initial eigenstate under the new Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Bures distance $B_A(t)$, which quantifies deviation from equilibrium; decay exponents $\lambda$ and $	ilde{\lambda}$; subsystem size scaling exponent $\alpha$.
important_parameters: Pre-quench field ($h_0$), post-quench field ($h$), and the properties of the symmetric excitation-fraction function $m_S(\varphi)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on numerical studies across various parameter regimes, and while robust, a complete analytical derivation for all exponents is pending.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative $(h_0, h)$ pairs covering distinct physical regimes; flowcharts guide the determination of $\lambda$ based on the continuity and differentiability of $m_S(\varphi)$; numerical plots confirm power-law decay with discrete exponents.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the model and quench protocol, then classifies representative field pairs $(h_0, h)$ using flowcharts derived from the analytic properties of the excitation function $m_S(\varphi)$, culminating in the presentation of the main results on discrete power-law decay.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep quantitative understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics in integrable quantum systems, offering universal rules for how local information spreads and thermalizes after a sudden change in Hamiltonian parameters.
